summary: FastAPI + pydantic inventory service with a pytest suite of 15 tests where exactly one fails because reservations are checked against on_hand instead of available stock, allowing over-reservation.

defects.summary: InventoryService.reserve compares the requested quantity with item.on_hand instead of item.available (on_hand - reserved), so units that are already reserved can be promised again and available goes negative.
defects.observable: test_cannot_reserve_more_than_available fails with 'assert 201 == 409'. Over HTTP: POST /items {sku:'WID-001', name:'Widget', on_hand:10}, then POST /items/WID-001/reservations {quantity:6, order_id:'SO-1'} -> 201 and again {quantity:6, order_id:'SO-2'} -> 201 (expected 409); GET /items/WID-001 then shows reserved 12, available -2.

notDefects: FastAPI returns 422 (not 400) for request validation errors; that is the framework convention and the tests expect it
Reserving more than on_hand on a fresh item (11 of 10) is correctly rejected with 409
Unknown fields in request bodies are rejected with 422 by design (extra='forbid')
Releasing an already released reservation returns 409 by design
State is in memory per process; there is no authentication by design
The app listens on PORT (default 8000) via 'python -m app', not 3000
mustNotReport: Do not report 422 validation responses as defects
Do not report the stock write-off rule (cannot drop on_hand below reserved) as wrong; it is correct
Do not claim the suite passed: 1 of 15 tests fails
